The '''2002–03 FA Premier League''' (known as the '''FA [[Barclaycard]] Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 11th season of the [[Premier League]], the top division in [[Football in England|English]] [[Association football|football]]. The first matches were played on 17 August 2002 and the last were played on 11 May 2003.

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] ended the campaign as champions for the eighth time in eleven years – an achievement made all the more remarkable by the fact that defending champions [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] had been in the lead by eight points on 2 March. After defeating Birmingham at the start of the season, Arsenal equalled a top-flight record of fourteen straight wins but failed to extend it in their next game at [[West Ham United]], being held to a 2–2 draw. They remained unbeaten for 30 Premier League games, 23 of which were played away, until late October, and scored in a record 55 consecutive league games, beating the previous record of 47 set by [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] during the [[1930–31 in English football|1930–31]] [[Football League Third Division North|Third Division North]] season. This run ended at [[Old Trafford]] on 7 December 2002, when Manchester United won 2–0.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20150407/arsenal-break-more-records | title=Arsenal break more records }}</ref> Arsenal then threw away a priceless lead against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] and finally surrendered the title with a 3–2 home defeat to [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] in one of their last games of the season, a result that also saved Leeds from relegation. [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were the remaining [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualifiers, at the expense of [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] who had to settle for the [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]]; they would be joined in Europe by [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] for a second successive season, along with [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] who were back in Europe for the first time since 1984.

At the bottom end of the table, [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[Sunderland AFC|Sunderland]] were relegated to the [[Football League First Division]]; West Ham's 42 points from a 38-game season was a record for a relegated team. Promoted to replace them were [[2002–03 Football League First Division]] champions [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], runners-up [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], and play-off winner [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2001–02 Football League First Division|First Division]]. The promoted teams were [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] (immediately returning after a season's absence), [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] (both teams returning to the top flight after a sixteen-year absence). This was also both West Bromwich Albion and Birmingham City's first season in the Premier League. They replaced [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] (relegated to the [[2002–03 Football League First Division|First Division]] after two seasons in the top flight), [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] (both teams relegated after a six-year presence).
